quizTitle: Project Management - Module 5: WBS & WBS Dictionary

questions.text: What does a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) do?
options: Breaks a large project into smaller, manageable, deliverable-oriented work packages
Lists every meeting the team will hold during the project
Assigns salaries and budgets to each team member
questions.explanation: A WBS breaks a massive, overwhelming project into smaller, manageable, deliverable-oriented pieces (work packages), so every team member understands the exact scope and duplication and ambiguity are eliminated.

questions.text: In the course plan, which week and topic does the WBS & WBS Dictionary module fall under?
questions.explanation: The module is aligned with Week 8 - Scope Management. Week 9 (the next topic) is Project Quality Management.

questions.text: In which assessment is the WBS tested as an essential core deliverable?
questions.explanation: The course plan alignment lists the WBS as an essential core deliverable tested in Long Test 2.

questions.text: The WBS is a mandatory structural prerequisite for the final (capstone) Project Management Plan submission.
questions.explanation: True. The course plan lists the WBS as a mandatory structural prerequisite for the final Project Management Plan submission.

questions.text: In PMBOK standards, which three components make up the Scope Baseline? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The Scope Baseline trio is the Approved Scope Statement + WBS + WBS Dictionary. The WBS is 1 of these 3 core components.

questions.text: Match each Scope Baseline component to its description.
allChoices: Detailed textual description of project scope, major deliverables, core assumptions, and critical boundaries/constraints
Deliverable-oriented hierarchical decomposition illustrating the entire total scope of work
Supporting document detailing operational descriptions, acceptance criteria, cost, and owners for each package

pairs.match: Detailed textual description of project scope, major deliverables, core assumptions, and critical boundaries/constraints
Deliverable-oriented hierarchical decomposition illustrating the entire total scope of work
Supporting document detailing operational descriptions, acceptance criteria, cost, and owners for each package

questions.explanation: The Scope Statement describes scope in text, the WBS decomposes it hierarchically, and the WBS Dictionary documents the details of each work package.

questions.text: What does the "Golden Rule" (100% Rule) of the WBS state?
options: The WBS must encompass 100% of the work defined by the project scope, no more and no less
Each work package must be 100% complete before the next one starts
100% of the team must approve the WBS before it is used
Every work package must take exactly 100 hours
questions.explanation: The WBS must encompass 100% of the work defined by the project scope, including internal, external, and project management work: no more, no less.

questions.text: Under the 100% Rule, project management work itself is excluded from the WBS because it is not a technical deliverable.
questions.explanation: False. The 100% Rule explicitly includes internal, external, and project management tasks. In the example, 1.1 Project Management & Governance is its own branch.

questions.text: Per the 100% Rule: if a deliverable is not in the WBS, it is officially out of ___.
questions.explanation: A key takeaway: if a deliverable is not in the WBS, it is officially out of scope.

questions.text: In the Cloud Banking Application Migration example, under which Level 2 element does "1.2.2 OAuth2 Single Sign-On Integration" belong?
questions.context:
1.0 Cloud Banking Application Migration
├── 1.1 Project Management & Governance
│   ├── 1.1.1 Project Charter & Planning Documents
│   └── 1.1.2 Stakeholder Communication Reports
├── 1.2 User Authentication Module
│   ├── 1.2.1 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Engine
│   └── 1.2.2 OAuth2 Single Sign-On Integration
├── 1.3 Core Financial Services
│   ├── 1.3.1 Account Balance API
│   └── 1.3.2 Real-time Fund Transfer Engine [Work Package]
└── 1.4 Cloud Infrastructure & Security
    ├── 1.4.1 AWS Production Environment Provisioning
    └── 1.4.2 Database Encryption & PCI-DSS Compliance
questions.explanation: The code 1.2.2 means it is the second child of 1.2, the User Authentication Module.

questions.text: In the Cloud Banking example, which element is marked as the work package detailed in the WBS Dictionary entry?
questions.explanation: 1.3.2 Real-time Fund Transfer Engine is labeled the work package (the lowest-level deliverable) and has a full WBS Dictionary entry.

questions.text: What is a work package?
options: The lowest-level deliverable in the WBS
The root (Level 1) element of the WBS
A folder that stores project documents
The list of team members on the project
questions.explanation: A work package is the lowest-level deliverable in the WBS, and it is the level documented in the WBS Dictionary.

questions.text: Match each field of the WBS Dictionary entry for 1.3.2 to its value.
allChoices: RESTful microservices for interbank fund transfers adhering to ISO 20022 message formats

pairs.match: RESTful microservices for interbank fund transfers adhering to ISO 20022 message formats

questions.explanation: The WBS Dictionary entry for 1.3.2 Real-time Fund Transfer Engine lists these field values.

questions.text: Which of the following are acceptance criteria listed for the 1.3.2 Real-time Fund Transfer Engine? (Select all that apply.)
options: End-to-end processing latency < 1.5 seconds per transaction under peak load
100% compliance with ISO 20022 audit logging standards
Zero critical vulnerabilities in automated static and dynamic security scans
At least 1,000 downloads in the first month
questions.explanation: The three acceptance criteria are latency < 1.5 seconds under peak load, 100% ISO 20022 audit-logging compliance, and zero critical vulnerabilities in automated security scans. All three are objective and testable.

questions.text: What is Anti-Pattern #1, the "Task-List" Trap?
options: Naming WBS elements with verbs (actions) instead of nouns (deliverables)
Including project management work in the WBS
questions.explanation: The Task-List Trap uses verbs instead of nouns (e.g. "Write Python Code", "Test Code", "Fix Bugs"). It focuses on ongoing actions and makes tracking baseline completion impossible.

questions.text: Which of these are correctly written as deliverable-oriented (noun-based) WBS elements? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Auth Microservice, Test Execution Report, and Staging Deployment are nouns with a clear output that can be definitively accepted. "Write Python Code" and "Fix Bugs" are verb-based actions.

questions.text: Match each decomposition anti-pattern to its size threshold and consequence.
allChoices: < 8 hours: massive administrative overhead, micro-management fatigue, tracking complexity
> 80 hours: "blind spots" where cost overruns and schedule delays stay hidden until too late

pairs.match: < 8 hours: massive administrative overhead, micro-management fatigue, tracking complexity
> 80 hours: "blind spots" where cost overruns and schedule delays stay hidden until too late

questions.explanation: Work packages under 8 hours are over-decomposed; over 80 hours are under-decomposed. Well-sized packages fall between the two.

questions.text: A team's work package is estimated at 150 hours. Which anti-pattern is this, and what is the risk?
options: Under-decomposition: cost overruns and delays can stay hidden until too late
The Task-List Trap: the element is named with a verb
No anti-pattern: larger packages are always better
questions.explanation: Anything over 80 hours is under-decomposed, creating blind spots where cost overruns and schedule delays remain hidden until too late.

questions.text: Match each aspect to the Predictive (Waterfall WBS) or Adaptive (Agile Backlog) approach.

pairs.term: Comprehensive upfront planning before execution begins
Formal Change Request via a Change Control Board (CCB)
Product Backlog re-prioritization before each Sprint

questions.explanation: Waterfall uses a WBS → Control Account → Work Package hierarchy, plans upfront, and controls scope through a CCB. Agile uses Epic → Feature → User Story, elaborates progressively, and re-prioritizes the backlog each Sprint.

questions.text: Which kind of project is the Predictive (Waterfall WBS) approach best suited for?
options: Fixed scope, highly regulated compliance, or infrastructure projects
Rapidly evolving digital products and mobile apps
SaaS solutions with frequent feature changes
Projects with no defined scope at all
questions.explanation: Predictive suits fixed scope, highly regulated compliance, or infrastructure projects. Adaptive suits rapidly evolving digital products, mobile apps, and SaaS.

questions.text: In the Grocery Mobile App case study, Marketing informally requests an AI-driven Recommendation Engine in Week 3 and the lead developer starts building it immediately. What is this called?
questions.explanation: The AI Engine isn't in the scope baseline/WBS, so unapproved work underway is classic scope creep.

questions.text: In the Grocery Mobile App case study, what is the correct PM decision?
options: Let the developer continue since Marketing asked for it
Freeze the unapproved development and initiate a formal Change Request that evaluates cost and schedule impact
Silently add the feature to the WBS and extend the deadline
questions.explanation: The PM freezes unapproved dev immediately and initiates a formal Change Request evaluating the cost ($18k) and schedule (3 weeks) impact before approval.

questions.text: Match each Grocery Mobile App case figure to its value.

pairs.term: Estimated cost impact of the AI Engine
Estimated schedule impact of the AI Engine

questions.explanation: The project has a strict 4-month deadline and $120,000 budget. The AI Engine change request is evaluated at $18k and 3 weeks.

questions.text: What is the first step the PM takes in the case study when the new feature request surfaces?
options: Check the scope baseline & WBS to see whether the AI Engine is listed
Ask Marketing for a bigger budget
Move the deadline back by 3 weeks
questions.explanation: Step 1 is to check the scope baseline & WBS component tree. The AI Engine isn't listed, which identifies the risk as scope creep.

questions.text: Which WBS rules does this flawed breakdown violate? (Select all that apply.)
questions.context:
1.0 Campus Event Management System
├── 1.1 Talk to Student Council Representatives
├── 1.2 Design Database Schema & ERD
├── 1.3 Write Backend Code in Node.js
└── 1.4 Perform Integration Testing
options: It uses action verbs (Talk, Design, Write, Perform) instead of deliverable nouns
It omits project management work, so it doesn't cover 100% of the scope
It uses a decimal numbering scheme
It has a single root element at Level 1
questions.explanation: The slides' audit note flags the action verbs (the Task-List Trap). The tree also has no project management branch, so it can't cover 100% of the scope. Decimal numbering and a single root are both correct practice. (The slides leave the second error open as a discussion question, so this one is inferred from the 100% Rule.)

questions.text: Which is the best deliverable-oriented rewrite of "1.3 Write Backend Code in Node.js"?
questions.explanation: "Node.js Backend API" is a noun naming a tangible output that can be accepted. The others still describe actions.

questions.text: What topic comes next after this module (Week 9)?
questions.explanation: Week 9 is Project Quality Management: Quality Planning, QA vs. QC, and the 7 Basic Quality Tools.
